OUR CURRENT BATCH · LAGERING

Broken Rake
Fall Lager.

A campfire kind of beer.

We aimed for a pumpkin festbier. The mash had other opinions. What emerged was a bold, malty, amber lager that still says “fall” loud and clear.

This batch is spending a month lagering before we share it at November’s Pan de Campo festival in Weslaco. Brewed for the season of gathering with friends and family.

PACIFIC NORTHWEST ROOTS. SOUTH TEXAS SOUL.

Good company
has deep roots.

Beer for slow days, good company,
and wherever the trail leads.

lowcase Brewing started as an idea on the trails of the Pacific Northwest, where adventure is just around the next peak or switchback. We wanted to brew beer that connected people to the outdoors.

Today, lowcase Brewing has taken its first steps on the South Texas plains. We’re brewing beers that keep that connection to the outdoors, but also aim to build connections with friends and family.

Every batch is built with intention so that when someone cracks one open, it feels like it belongs exactly where they are.

We’re brewing beer
and building moments.

El Pescador:
The beer that started it all.

A generous helping of Vienna malt took our first pilsner idea somewhere unexpected—and gave lowcase Brewing its first family favorite.

BREW STORIES02
the mash had other opinions

Broken Rake:
The brew day had other plans.

We set out to brew a pumpkin festbier. An overpacked malt pipe led us somewhere unexpected: a bold, malty, amber lager with a gathering waiting at the other end.

Second Wind:
A little sour. A fresh start.

Sometimes you brew a beer just because you love it. Our traditional Berliner Weisse brings a bright, tart pause to a day out—and we’re skipping the syrup.

SECOND WIND BERLINER WEISSE

Trailhead Wit:
Too much fizz. A lesson worth keeping.

We aimed for sunshine in a glass. A batch of gushers sent us back to the notebook—with lessons to carry into the next brew day.
